Scope: 44 ready-built factories of 900 m² each in 11 blocks (B1–B11), with external utilities, roads, parking and street lighting.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours (225,786 man-hours in the P6 update). At the 24-Nov-2026 data date the project is 86.9% complete against 85.5% planned, 1.4% ahead. This week added 1.5% against 2.2% planned, so the lead over the plan narrowed from 2.1%. The weekly report workbook was again not uploaded, so the headline figures come from the progress presentation and the phase and block figures from the P6 update, which gives the same 86.89%.

Up to invoice 9 (01–15 Nov 2026)
Still ahead, but the lead narrowed and the forecast finish slipped two more days with no float left. The P6 update finishes the project on 27-Feb-2027, seven days before the contract completion date of 06-Mar-2027, with zero float on project completion. The civil works milestone slipped another week in P6, to 15-Dec-2026, and testing and commissioning moved a week to 13-Jan-2027. The milestone for site levelling, local roads and parking has still not started and is again forecast for the data date, now with 8 days of float. Gypsum board and the last key deliveries except the in-line toilet fans were completed this week.

Site photos this week

Six of the 18 photos uploaded this week, all stamped 24-Nov-2026 with the time and the project tag DAM3-05-11 (a map tag, no coordinates). The progress presentation of 24-Nov-2026 lists cladding in Blocks 6 and 7, painting of partition walls in Blocks 2, 3, 5 and 8, gypsum board partitions in Blocks 9 and 10, the telecom cabinet in Block 11, panels in Block 1, floor preparation for epoxy paint in Block 4, HVAC ducts in Block 6, and installation of the GRP tank and the fire pump. Civil works and testing slipped another week in P6; the project finish moved two days. Civil works moved seven days to 15-Dec-2026, 75 days after its P6 baseline of 01-Oct-2026, and testing and commissioning moved seven days to 13-Jan-2027. Mechanical works moved one day earlier to 05-Jan-2027 and electrical and architectural works two days earlier to 31-Jan-2027. Construction completion moved one day to 17-Feb-2027 and the project finish two days to 27-Feb-2027, still with zero float. The contractual milestone for site levelling, local roads and parking (P6 baseline 12-Feb-2026) has still not started; its float rose from 3 to 8 days.

Data notes

  • The weekly report workbook (WPR #40) was not uploaded for the second week running. The file DAM3-05-11_WPR40_2026-11-24.xlsx is the procurement tracker, byte-identical to the files uploaded in the two previous weeks. No checklist, submittal register or look-ahead was uploaded. Planned values per phase and block, the milestone sheet, monthly manpower, the invoice log and HSE statistics for this week are therefore missing.
  • Headline planned and actual progress come from the progress presentation (85.49% and 86.89%). Phase and block figures were computed from the P6 update: each activity's physical % complete weighted by its budgeted labour hours. This method gives 86.89% this week, the same as the presentation.
  • Week number: no contract week is stated this week. Week 46 continues the contract-week count of WPR #37 (week 43 at 03-Nov-2026); (24-Nov-2026 − 07-Jan-2026) // 7 gives 45, because contract weeks count from 1.
  • Invoicing: the presentation moved from invoice 7 (01–31 Oct 2026, 50,050,337 SAR) last week to invoice 9 (01–15 Nov 2026, 59,763,199.62 SAR) this week; invoice 8 is not described. The presentation also shows a value-based percentage for executed works, which is not a physical measure and is not used here.
  • Quality figures in the presentation: FIRs 1,160 submitted, 1,011 closed and 49 remaining, which do not add up (149). NCRs show 16 issued with 1 open but also 16 closed; last week no NCR was open.
  • Risk & Issue log: the dashboard shows 242 open risks and 128 open issues, against 3 open risks and no open issues in the logs. RISK-003 (fire hose cabinets) still says the risk relates to a future activity although installation has started.
  • The log names Engr Hamdi as MODON PM, while WPR #38 names Engr. Affat Al-Enezi as MODON PM.
  • The manpower and equipment figures in the presentation are unchanged since 05-Nov-2026. Safe man-hours rose by 16,200 this week after four weeks of exactly 16,440.
  • The presentation's gypsum board unit is "Item"; its quantities are in m². Its revised total (12,432.64) is almost three times the original 4,425.
  • The P6 project code is now DAM3-05-11_WPR40, but its planned start is still 14-Mar-2023.
